name: Alexandrian research library
description: A Ptolemaic scholarly library associated with the Museum in Alexandria, used to collect and study writings.

impact.note: State-funded collecting and study of all available writings gave Mediterranean scholars a new way of working; textual scholarship and later research libraries grew from it.

date.label: third century BCE
date.basis: Date or stated historical interval in cited source; see caveats.

events.statement: A Ptolemaic ruler created a library and Museum for scholars in Alexandria during the third century BCE.
events.caveats: UCL leaves uncertain whether Ptolemy I or II founded it, the terms of access and the full scope of holdings.

evidence.supports: UCL dates creation of the Museum and library to the third century BCE, uncertain between Ptolemy I and II.

earliest_record.rationale: The cited institutional account gives an estimated third-century BCE foundation, not the date of the earliest independently secure surviving witness.

links.statement: The library held writings on papyrus scrolls, using a papyrus writing medium.
links.scope: The functional medium represented by the Egyptian papyrus record; no transmission, descent from the surviving blank roll, or exact foundation holdings are established.

evidence.supports: UNESCO describes the library’s papyrus scrolls.
The Met explains the papyrus roll writing medium.

caveats: Access beyond associated scholars, exact holdings and the date or cause of loss are unresolved; earlier libraries and archives existed. The earliest securely dated documentary witness is not established by this source; the foundation date is a historical reconstruction. Collection-size figures are not established.

research.note: Initial sourced research; independent review pending. Independent reader checked UCL account; founder, holdings, and access remain uncertain.
